data.description: Du willst Software bauen, die echte Menschen jeden Tag nutzen und nicht das zwölfte Ticket in einem Konzern abarbeiten? Dann komm zu Matelify. Wir sind ein Startup aus Rödental bei Coburg. Mit Matelify helfen wir Unternehmen, auf Social Media nicht nur zu posten, sondern es zu verstehen. Herzstück sind unsere Mates: fünf KI-Agenten: Cleo erstellt Content, Finn plant, Nova denkt Strategie, Alex analysiert, Max kümmert sich um die Community. Sie arbeiten im Chat live zusammen und beraten sich gegenseitig. Diese Zusammenarbeit ist das Produkt. Jetzt suchen wir dich als Software Engineer in Vollzeit. Jemanden, der Features von der Idee bis in Produktion trägt. Was du bei uns machst Du baust Features end-to-end: Datenmodell, API, Oberfläche, Deployment, Messung. Kein Weiterreichen über drei Teams. Du entwickelst unsere KI-Agenten weiter: von Tools und Prompts bis hin zu Orchestrierung und Evaluation. Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Mates immer smarter, zuverlässiger und besser im Zusammenspiel werden. Du arbeitest in einer echten Cloud-Architektur: Go-Services auf AWS, serverless, Infrastruktur als Code. Du schaust nach dem Release auf die Daten: Wird das Feature genutzt? Wo steigen Leute aus? Und baust danach weiter. Du gestaltest nicht nur mit, wie wir etwas entwickeln, sondern auch, was wir bauen. Dabei bringst du eigene Ideen ein und tauschst dich direkt mit unseren Kunden aus, um ihre Bedürfnisse besser zu verstehen. Du entwickelst unsere Plattform kontinuierlich weiter mit automatisierten Tests, CI/CD und Observability. Dabei sorgst du für sauberen Code, stabile Prozesse und eine Architektur, die mit uns wächst. Kurz gesagt: Du bist kein Ressourcen-Slot im Sprint, sondern baust das Produkt mit. Unser Stack Frontend: TypeScript, React Backend: Go-Microservices auf AWS, MongoDB, Python Infra & Ops: Terraform, GitLab, CI/CD Du musst nicht alles davon kennen. Aber du solltest Lust haben, dich in jeden Teil einzuarbeiten. Wie wir arbeiten KI ist bei uns Werkzeug, kein Buzzword. Wir entwickeln selbst mit KI-Coding-Agents im Alltag und erwarten, dass du damit souverän umgehst. Schnell sein ist gut. Verstehen, was da generiert wurde, ist Pflicht. Ownership statt Zuständigkeit. Wer etwas baut, kümmert sich auch darum, dass es läuft. Kurze Wege. Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Founder-Team. Entscheidungen dauern Minuten, nicht Wochen. Shippen schlägt Perfektion, aber mit Tests, Code-Review und grüner Pipeline. Hybrid & flexibel: Du entscheidest, wo du am produktivsten arbeitest, von zu Hause oder gemeinsam mit dem Team in Rödental. Was du mitbringst Studium, Ausbildung, Quereinstieg, egal was, es ist uns egal. Uns interessiert, ob du Software verstehst, Bock hast und zeigen kannst, was du draufhast. Wichtig ist uns: Du hast mehrere Jahre echte Praxis in der Softwareentwicklung: ob im Job, in eigenen Projekten oder Open Source und hast Features eigenständig in Produktion gebracht und danach betreut. Du bist sehr sicher in TypeScript und/oder Go und arbeitest dich schnell in den jeweils anderen Teil ein. Du triffst Architekturentscheidungen selbst, kannst sie begründen und weißt, wann „gut genug“ wirklich gut genug ist. Du verstehst, wie Web-Apps funktionieren: APIs, Datenbanken, Auth, Deployments. Du hast mit LLMs oder Agenten schon mehr gemacht als einen Chatbot gefragt oder brennst darauf, genau das zu tun. Du kommunizierst klar und sprichst sehr gut Deutsch und Englisch, mündlich wie schriftlich. Ein Plus, kein Muss: AWS/Serverless, Terraform, MongoDB, Produktanalytics, Erfahrung in einem frühen Startup. Du erfüllst nicht jeden Punkt? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Was wir dir bieten Echte Produktverantwortung in einem wachsenden KI-Produkt Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit dem Founder-/CEO-Team Moderner Stack und Raum, ihn mitzuprägen Ein kleines, motiviertes Team ohne Politik und Meeting-Marathons Viel Raum für eigene Ideen: die beste Idee gewinnt, nicht die lauteste Hybrides Arbeiten und flexible Arbeitszeiten So bewirbst du dich Schick uns: deinen Lebenslauf oder ein gepflegtes LinkedIn-Profil einen Link zu etwas, das du gebaut hast (GitHub, GitLab, Projekt, Demo) Kein Anschreiben, keine Zeugnisse, kein Notenschnitt. Uns interessiert, wie du denkst und was du gebaut hast. Unser Prozess: kurzes Kennenlernen → technisches Gespräch über echten Code statt Leetcode-Rätsel → persönliches Kennenlernen mit dem Team vor Ort in Rödental. Wir freuen uns auf dich! data.description: Role - Software Engineer - Optimisation Team Company - iwell - Harmonizing Clean Energy Location - Utrecht About iwell At iwell, we are all about reinforcing energy security. We help European businesses become more energy independent. With growing regulations, extreme price volatility and rising grid issues, they need to be resilient. It is time to take charge and think ahead. We deliver energy management solutions that ensure that businesses are always in control of their energy. Our in-house developed EMS and modular battery storage drive profit through sustainability, making businesses future-proof. We are a fast-growing international team of bold, talented individuals. From engineers and software developers to creative thinkers and customer-focused business developers. No matter what your strong suit is, we always are looking for people who are determined to make a positive impact. The Role The Optimisation team builds the Python applications that decide what our customers' energy assets should do, and when. Batteries, EV fleets, solar and grid connections all come together in our optimiser, and the team turns prices, forecasts and constraints into schedules and decisions that run in production every day. Much of this work has an operations-research flavour, and the problems rarely arrive neatly defined.. They arrive as a customer who needs their vans charged by 6:00 at the lowest cost or a battery whose value depends on the hour. We're looking for someone who is comfortable across that whole path: understanding the real-world problem, shaping it into something a computer can solve, and shipping and operating the result. You don't need to be an OR specialist. You do need to be a strong Python engineer who enjoys messy, concrete problems. Success in this role means being able to: Take a loosely defined operational problem and turn it into working, maintainable production code. Work with data and models (optimisation, forecasting or plain statistics) without losing sight of the engineering. What you will do Create charging schedules for EV fleets that minimise electricity costs while guaranteeing every vehicle is ready when it needs to be. This means modelling tariffs, grid limits and departure times, and handling what happens when reality deviates from the plan. Calculate the value of each kWh produced or consumed, so that batteries, solar and flexible loads are steered by what energy is actually worth at that moment, and customers can see where their savings come from. Build forecasting models that predict operational issues before they happen, to maximise asset uptime and reduce the number of support tickets our Operations team has to handle. Take your work all the way to production: packaging, deployment, monitoring and bugfixing. Work with the rest of the Optimisation team on the shared tooling, data pipelines and modelling conventions the team uses.. What are looking for 5+ years of production Python development experience, writing clean, tested, maintainable code. A proven ability to translate real-world problems into working code. Data analysis experience Energy, battery or electricity domain knowledge: tariffs, grid constraints, day-ahead and imbalance markets. The willingness to take on a People lead role in the team. data.description: This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. If you've built something before, start here The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day. What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you. About Scalera Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day. What you'll do You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with. Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket. Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved. Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on. Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate. Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix. Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people. What success looks like after 3 months There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it You'll probably thrive here if You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls You make things simpler over time, not more clever You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement You probably won't enjoy it if You just want to code and go home You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit Ambiguity and chaos bother you You want a well-defined backlog handed to you Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount Our stack Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one. How we hire Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions. Technical deep-dive call: walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong. Meet Scalera Day: join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team. Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer. Working at Scalera Remote within the EU or EEA Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success Competitive compensation Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on.
